<!-- Tables 1 and 2 for the manuscript, as EDITABLE Word tables.

     2026-10-08: renamed from ms/fig_tbl/table1.qmd (its build outputs are now
     main_tables.docx and, in a revision build, ms/revision/main_tables_{marked,clean}.docx);
     Table 2 no longer prints Missing rows (decision 45), so its legend no longer mentions
     missing data.

     2026-10-07 (reviewer round, R1.2 and R2.2): Table 2 (baseline characteristics by group,
     merging the submitted Tables S1 and S2) is added after Table 1. It is built in
     demographics/05_table2_baseline.qmd as a flextable with a FIXED layout for a landscape
     page, and printed here from its saved object. The document's body section is landscape
     (reference-doc above); a raw section break after the Table 1 legend keeps Table 1 on a
     portrait page. In the marked build (REV_MODE=marked, exported by
     ms/revision/build_revision.sh) Table 2 is shaded as a whole, because it is new, and
     (since 2026-10-13, round 6) Table 1 is shaded cell by cell and footnote by footnote where it
     differs from Table 1 as submitted (ms/submission/table1.docx; chunk `submitted`).
     Table 1 now uses a fixed layout too: flextable's autofit layout writes no w:tblGrid,
     which the Word schema requires (pandoc then read the table as rows without cells).

     Original note (Table 1):

     Alzheimer's & Dementia returned ADJ-D-26-02882 asking for tables "in editable
     text format (.docx) as opposed to an image". Every table in this tree is a
     gtsave() PNG, so the main table is rebuilt here from the gt object its producer
     already saves alongside the PNG (demographics/01_dementia_category_table.qmd:190
     writes both). Renders to DOCX ONLY.

     The supplementary tables stay images and travel inside
     ms/fig_tbl/supplementary_tables.qmd -> suppl_figures_tables.pdf, which the
     journal's own bullet allows ("only one file of each type" explicitly lists .pdf).

     WHY flextable AND NOT gt's OWN WORD WRITER. `gt::as_word()` produced a file Word
     on macOS could not open properly (reported 2026-08-31). Two defects, both
     confirmed in the emitted XML:
       - `cell_text(size = 6)` in the producer is SIX PIXELS in gt's HTML/PNG world,
         but as_word() passes the number straight through as `w:sz`, which is in
         HALF-POINTS -- so the table body rendered at 3 pt.
       - 38 elements were ISO-29500 *Strict* spellings (`w:start`/`w:end` inside
         `w:tcBorders` and `w:tblCellMar`) and 35 `w:jc` values were `start`/`end`,
         none of which are legal in the *transitional* schema this .docx declares.
     flextable writes transitional, Word-native markup; verified after this render:
     zero `w:start`/`w:end`, `w:jc` only left/right/center, one font size.

     Rendering the gt as raw HTML and letting Quarto build the table was tried first
     and does NOT work: Quarto's raw-HTML-table processing did not fire, and every
     cell came out as its own paragraph with no <w:tbl> at all.

     THE FLOAT-KIND HAZARD IS CONTAINED, NOT AVOIDED. Emitting a table from an R chunk
     rather than as `![](png){#tbl-...}` changes the float's Quarto kind, and a kind
     change is what once produced "Table S1...S11 with no Table 1". This document holds
     two main tables, defined in the same order as their stubs in _pseudo_figures.qmd
     (tbl-dementia-category, then tbl-baseline), and ms/_metadata.yml was not touched --
     but confirm it renders "Table 1" and "Table 2".

     The div wrapper (rather than a chunk `#| label:`) is what keeps the cross-reference
     target. Quarto emits the wrapper as a <w:tbl> holding an ImageCaption paragraph
     whose whole text is "Table 1"; ms/post_process_docx.py strips that, because the
     hand-written legend below already opens with it. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
# tidyverse, here and stringr come from .Rprofile.
pacman::p_load(gt, flextable, install = FALSE)

g <- read_rds(here("demographics/output/dementia_category_table_base.rds"))

# Everything below is DERIVED from that object -- cell values, column labels,
# footnote texts and footnote marker numbers. Nothing is retyped, so a change in
# demographics/01 reaches this table instead of silently disagreeing with the PNG
# the slide deck shows. The stopifnot()s below fail loudly if an assumption breaks.

# gt marks a footnoted cell by appending an HTML <sup>; extract_body() hands those
# back verbatim, so the marker numbers gt itself assigned are readable here.
MARK <- "<span[^>]*>\\s*<sup>(\\d+)</sup>\\s*</span>"
mark_of  <- \(x) as.integer(str_match(x, MARK)[, 2])
strip_of <- \(x) str_remove_all(x, MARK)

body_raw <- gt::extract_body(g)
boxhead  <- g[["_boxhead"]]

# Visible columns, in display order: the stub first, then the default columns in
# the order gt lays them out (`cols_move()` in the producer put followup_mean
# before count, and _boxhead already reflects that).
vis    <- boxhead[boxhead$type %in% c("stub", "default"), ]
vis    <- vis[order(match(vis$type, c("stub", "default")), seq_len(nrow(vis))), ]
cols   <- vis$var
labels <- setNames(as.character(vis$column_label), cols)
labels[[cols[1]]] <- ""          # the stub column has no header in the gt
stopifnot("expected 5 visible columns" = length(cols) == 5)

# extract_body() does NOT key the stub column by its variable name -- it renames it
# to the literal "::rowname::". Reading it as `transition` silently returns NULL, so
# the stub's own footnote markers (3 and 6) vanish and only the two data markers are
# seen. Checked rather than assumed, because a gt release could rename it again.
STUB_SRC <- "::rowname::"
stopifnot("gt renamed the stub column in extract_body()" = STUB_SRC %in% names(body_raw))
src_col <- \(cl) if (cl == cols[1]) STUB_SRC else cl
```

```{r}
#| label: footnotes
#| echo: false
fns <- g[["_footnotes"]]

# gt numbers footnotes by first appearance, header row before body. So the
# column-label footnotes take 1..k in column order, and the body markers start at
# k+1 -- which is checked, not assumed, against the numbers extract_body() emitted.
hdr_fns <- fns[fns$locname == "columns_columns", ]
hdr_fns <- hdr_fns[order(match(hdr_fns$colname, cols)), ]
k       <- nrow(hdr_fns)
hdr_mark <- setNames(seq_len(k), hdr_fns$colname)

body_marks <- unlist(lapply(cols, \(cl) mark_of(body_raw[[src_col(cl)]])))
body_marks <- sort(unique(body_marks[!is.na(body_marks)]))
stopifnot(
  "body footnote markers must start right after the header ones" =
    min(body_marks) == k + 1,
  "footnote markers must be contiguous from 1" =
    identical(c(seq_len(k), body_marks), seq_len(k + length(body_marks)))
)

# marker number -> footnote text, for the block under the table.
fn_text <- character(k + length(body_marks))
fn_text[seq_len(k)] <- as.character(hdr_fns$footnotes)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fns))) {
  loc <- fns$locname[i]
  if (loc == "columns_columns") next
  cl <- if (loc == "stub") cols[1] else as.character(fns$colname[i])
  m  <- mark_of(body_raw[[src_col(cl)]][fns$rownum[i]])
  if (!is.na(m)) fn_text[m] <- as.character(fns$footnotes[i])
}
stopifnot("every footnote marker must have text" = all(nzchar(fn_text)))
```

```{r}
#| label: submitted
#| echo: false
# Marked build only (REV_MODE=marked, exported by ms/revision/build_revision.sh): Table 1 is
# highlighted where it differs from Table 1 AS SUBMITTED (ms/submission/table1.docx, uploaded
# 2026-09-01), cell by cell and footnote by footnote, so that the Marked Revision shows what
# changed for the reviewers (added 2026-10-13, round 6). The clean build never reads that file.
marked <- identical(Sys.getenv("REV_MODE"), "marked")
cell_now <- \(txt, m) if (is.na(m)) txt else paste0(txt, m)
fn_norm  <- \(s) str_remove(str_squish(s), "[;.]$")
hl_header <- integer(0)
hl_body   <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = 0, ncol = 0)
fn_changed <- rep(FALSE, length(fn_text))

if (marked) {
  sub_path <- here("ms/submission/table1.docx")
  stopifnot("the as-submitted Table 1 is needed for the marked build" = file.exists(sub_path))
  sub_xml <- xml2::read_xml(unz(sub_path, "word/document.xml"))
  ns <- xml2::xml_ns(sub_xml)
  sub_tbl <- xml2::xml_find_all(sub_xml, "//w:tbl[count(w:tr) = 9]", ns)
  stopifnot("submitted Table 1: expected one table of 9 rows" = length(sub_tbl) == 1)
  sub_rows <- xml2::xml_find_all(sub_tbl[[1]], "w:tr", ns)
  cell_txt <- \(tc) str_squish(paste(xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_all(tc, ".//w:t", ns)),
                                      collapse = ""))
  sub_cells <- lapply(sub_rows[1:8], \(r) vapply(xml2::xml_find_all(r, "w:tc", ns), cell_txt, ""))
  stopifnot("submitted Table 1: expected 5 cells in the header and body rows" =
              all(lengths(sub_cells) == length(cols)))

  # Its footnotes: the last row's runs, split at each superscript marker number.
  sub_fn <- character(0)
  for (r in xml2::xml_find_all(sub_rows[[9]], ".//w:r", ns)) {
    t <- paste(xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_all(r, "w:t", ns)), collapse = "")
    is_mark <- length(xml2::xml_find_all(r, "w:rPr/w:vertAlign[@w:val='superscript']", ns)) > 0 &&
      str_detect(t, "^\\s*\\d+\\s*$")
    if (is_mark) {
      sub_fn[as.integer(t)] <- ""
    } else if (length(sub_fn) > 0) {
      sub_fn[length(sub_fn)] <- paste0(sub_fn[length(sub_fn)], t)
    }
  }
  stopifnot("submitted Table 1: footnote count differs" = length(sub_fn) == length(fn_text))

  head_now <- vapply(cols, \(cl) cell_now(labels[[cl]], if (cl %in% names(hdr_mark))
    hdr_mark[[cl]] else NA), "")
  hl_header <- which(str_squish(head_now) != sub_cells[[1]])
  body_now <- sapply(seq_along(cols), \(jj) vapply(seq_len(nrow(body_raw)), \(ii)
    str_squish(cell_now(strip_of(body_raw[[src_col(cols[jj])]][ii]),
                        mark_of(body_raw[[src_col(cols[jj])]][ii]))), ""))
  stopifnot("submitted Table 1: body rows differ in number" =
              nrow(body_now) == length(sub_cells) - 2)   # less the header and the total row
  hl_body <- body_now != do.call(rbind, sub_cells[2:(nrow(body_now) + 1)])
  fn_changed <- fn_norm(fn_text) != fn_norm(sub_fn)
  message("Table 1 vs submitted: header cells ", paste(hl_header, collapse = ", "),
          "; body cells ", sum(hl_body), "; footnotes ", paste(which(fn_changed), collapse = ", "))
}
```

::: {#tbl-dementia-category}
```{r}
#| label: table
#| echo: false
# Plain text for the cells; the markers go back on as real superscript runs below.
body <- as.data.frame(lapply(cols, \(cl) strip_of(body_raw[[src_col(cl)]])),
                      col.names = cols, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# The grand summary row. The producer sums the (unformatted) count column, so the
# same sum is taken here rather than transcribing 2,491.
total <- sum(g[["_data"]][["count"]], na.rm = TRUE)
body[nrow(body) + 1, ] <- c("total", "—", "—", "—",
                            format(total, big.mark = ","))
n_body <- nrow(body) - 1L

ft <- flextable(body) |>
  set_header_labels(values = as.list(labels)) |>
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
  bold(j = 1, part = "body") |>
  align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") |>
  align(j = 2:5, align = "right", part = "all") |>
  align(j = 2:3, align = "left", part = "all") |>
  padding(padding.top = 2, padding.bottom = 2, part = "all") |>
  border_remove() |>
  hline_top(part = "header", border = officer::fp_border(width = 1)) |>
  hline_bottom(part = "header", border = officer::fp_border(width = 0.5)) |>
  hline(i = n_body, part = "body", border = officer::fp_border(width = 0.5)) |>
  hline_bottom(part = "body", border = officer::fp_border(width = 1))

# Re-attach gt's footnote markers as superscripts, header first then body.
for (cl in names(hdr_mark)) {
  ft <- compose(ft, j = which(cols == cl), part = "header",
                value = as_paragraph(labels[[cl]], as_sup(as.character(hdr_mark[[cl]]))))
}
for (jj in seq_along(cols)) {
  for (ii in seq_len(n_body)) {
    m <- mark_of(body_raw[[src_col(cols[jj])]][ii])
    if (is.na(m)) next
    ft <- compose(ft, i = ii, j = jj, part = "body",
                  value = as_paragraph(body[ii, jj], as_sup(as.character(m))))
  }
}

# Marked build: highlight the cells that differ from the submitted table (chunk above).
for (jj in hl_header) ft <- highlight(ft, j = jj, part = "header", color = "yellow")
for (ii in seq_len(nrow(hl_body))) {
  for (jj in which(hl_body[ii, ])) ft <- highlight(ft, i = ii, j = jj, part = "body", color = "yellow")
}

# One footnote block under the table, in marker order -- the same single wrapped
# line the gt prints (tab_options(footnotes.multiline = FALSE) in the producer). In the
# marked build, a footnote whose text changed since submission is highlighted.
chunks <- list()
for (m in seq_along(fn_text)) {
  fn_mark <- as_sup(as.character(m))
  fn_body <- paste0(" ", fn_text[m])
  if (fn_changed[m]) {
    fn_mark <- as_highlight(fn_mark, color = "yellow")
    fn_body <- as_highlight(fn_body, color = "yellow")
  }
  chunks <- c(chunks, list(fn_mark, fn_body, " "))
}
ft <- ft |>
  add_footer_lines(values = do.call(as_paragraph, chunks)) |>
  fontsize(size = 8, part = "footer") |>
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "footer") |>
  align(align = "left", part = "footer")

# Fixed layout with explicit widths (see the header note): one-line widths of the
# header and body, scaled down to the portrait text width less the 108-twip side cell
# margins of Quarto's one-cell float wrapper. The footer wraps, so it is left out.
budget_in <- 6.5 - 2 * 108 / 1440
w_in <- pmax(dim_pretty(ft, part = "header")$widths, dim_pretty(ft, part = "body")$widths)
if (sum(w_in) > budget_in) w_in <- w_in * budget_in / sum(w_in)
ft <- ft |>
  width(width = w_in) |>
  set_table_properties(layout = "fixed")

ft
```

:::

**[@tbl-dementia-category]** | **Dementia transition categories in the study population.** Distribution of 2,491 participants across six cognitive transition categories based on [the AGES-I and AGES-II examinations and on dementia surveillance to October 2015 (up to 13.4 years; Figure S1)]{.rev}. Categories include: stable normal ([participants with normal cognition at baseline who were not diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia]{.rev}), normal2mci (transition from normal cognition to mild cognitive impairment), stable_mci ([participants with MCI at baseline who did not develop dementia throughout the follow-up]{.rev}), normal2incid ([normal cognition at AGES-I followed by incident dementia]{.rev}), mci2incid (transition from MCI to incident dementia), and prevalent dementia (dementia present at baseline). Follow-up time is presented as mean (standard deviation) [in days and is defined differently by group]{.rev}.

```{=openxml}
<w:p><w:pPr><w:sectPr><w:pgSz w:w="12240" w:h="15840"/><w:pgMar w:top="1440" w:right="1440" w:bottom="1440" w:left="1440" w:header="720" w:footer="720" w:gutter="0"/><w:cols w:space="720"/></w:sectPr></w:pPr></w:p>
```
